en.title: Folding Paper to a Given Height and Width
en.description:
Each fold is made along a crease parallel to one side and need not be in the middle; it changes only the corresponding dimension, and the target size is not rotated. One fold can turn a length L into any length in [L/2,L). Find the minimum number of folds needed to reach exactly h1,w1.

The input/output format was compiled by this site.
en.input: One line with h w h1 w1. The original text guarantees h1≤h and w1≤w and gives no numeric upper bound; on this site all four are integers in 1..10⁹.
en.output: Output the minimum number of folds.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 0, and 8; in the first example, height 8 can be folded to 6 in one fold, so folds must not be restricted to folding exactly in half.
hints: For each dimension separately, find the smallest t such that target×2^t≥original, then add the two results; use integer doubling to avoid floating-point error.
